matches.quote: a localized defect level generically shows resonances at both polarities (resonant tunnelling plus tip-induced ionization in a double-barrier geometry), and these shift and change intensity ratio with tip height
The abstract and introduction frame the work as revealing "how macroscopic coherence emerges from locally collapsed pairing" ... but no data near the excitonic transition are presented.
Defect-bound states of a topological insulator are a further alternative, since the material has been discussed as a quantum spin Hall and topological excitonic insulator (refs. 22, 25).
report the local gap magnitude, gap edges and gap center in type-I and type-II regions from many spectra (a locally reduced order parameter should give a smaller gap)
give statistics on how many defects of each type were measured in each region and how many type-II defects show the lower-energy states
The Te-vacancy identification rests on topography alone. VTe1–VTe4 are assigned from the apparent morphology ... They appear as "elongated protrusions", which is unusual for a missing chalcogen atom.
No DFT-simulated STM images, formation-energy arguments or controlled creation/annealing are presented. ... The authors should add simulated topographs (including defect-induced LDOS)
The relation to Kwon et al. (ref. 41) is handled only in a "Note added". A short discussion of what agrees and what differs ... would help readers.
Nothing in the data or model separates excitonic pair breaking from ordinary defect levels in a non-excitonic, hybridization-gapped insulator or semiconductor, and the Conclusion's logic is circular.
The ordering VTe2 → VTe4 → VTe1 → VTe3, claimed to reflect coupling strength, has no microscopic support.
The caption should say unambiguously which region is which, and type-I/type-II should be labelled on the map.
The model's bands are not shown to represent Ta2Pd3Te5's quasi-1D, multi-orbital, spin-orbit-coupled band structure, including its proposed Dirac/topological character (refs. 6, 22).
show whether the gap edges and coherence-like peak of a defect-free region shift over the same It sequence, which is the band-bending reference
Language and references need correcting: "formulism" → "formalism"; "predicated" → "predicted" (p. 5); "Yu-Yhiba-Rusinov" → "Yu-Shiba-Rusinov" (ref. 37); "those … tends"
The paper does not say how many crystals, cleaves and tips the key observations (Figs. 2e, 2g, 3, 4e) come from ... Because tip state strongly affects these spectra

For C15, P10 and P12 raise defect charging and ionization in a tip-defect-sample double-barrier junction producing sharp threshold peaks/rings, which is scored as 'partly' against dynamical Coulomb blockade.
